 Clergy Can Earn a Compass Retirement Match on Student Loan Payments
November 19, 2026 
 Louisiana Conference clergy who participate in the Compass Retirement Plan can earn matching retirement contributions from the church they serve based on qualifying student loan payments.
To receive the match for payments made in 2026, clergy must certify those payments in Benefits Access by January 31, 2027 .
 Student Loan FAQ's 
 How the Match Works 
Under a provision made possible by the SECURE 2.0 Act of 2022, Compass treats qualifying student loan payments like personal retirement contributions when calculating the match.
You can earn a dollar-for-dollar match of up to 4% of your plan compensation through your personal Compass contributions, qualifying student loan payments, or a combination of the two. 
For example, if your annual plan compensation is $50,000, a $1,000 personal Compass contribution and $1,000 in qualifying student loan payments would together earn the full $2,000 match. That matching contribution goes into your Compass retirement account.
 How to Certify Your 2026 Payments 
 Sign in to Benefits Access .
 ​Under Retirement , select Accounts . Then choose Student Loan Matching from the Contributions menu.
 Enter your lender’s name and your loan account number.
 Enter the date and amount of each qualifying payment you made in 2026. Record each payment individually.
 Watch for a confirmation email and keep your loan statements and payment records. 
Wespath says matching contributions for certified 2026 payments will be credited to Compass accounts by February 28, 2027 . For details on which loans qualify and how to report your payments, see Wespath’s student loan matching FAQ .
